newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China's accession to WTO said extremely important.
newsitem.headline: China's accession to WTO said extremely important.

text.p: The question of China's accession to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) has drifted off the political agenda but should be put back on it very soon, Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Saturday.
Fischer, who is also Minister for Trade, told reporters during a brief stopover in Singapore: "It is an extremely important issue."
He said he supported in principle China's accession to the WTO. "Negotiations are about to commence again in Geneva and I'd like to see an improvement in the progress with those negotiations."
Fischer said he wanted to see "sooner rather than later" a package of arrangements that would allow China's entry into the WTO.
He said arrangements could not be completed in time for this December's WTO Ministerial meeting in Singapore.
"Nevertheless, it is my hope that during that month and at the Singapore ministerial round... there will be real progress with regard to China," he said.
